results.bound: Swap, Replace, Delete, and Add are linearly equivalent for ISM and ISM-T
results.quote: Theorem 1. Swap, Replace, Delete, and Add are linearly equivalent for ISM and ISM-T.

results.bound: NP-hard and W[1]-hard when parameterized by k+b+|\mathcal{P}_1\oplus\mathcal{P}_2|
results.quote: Theorem 2. IASM is NP-hard and W[1]-hard when parameterized by k+b+|\mathcal{P}_1\oplus\mathcal{P}_2|.

results.bound: XP when parameterized by k or b or |\mathcal{P}_1\oplus\mathcal{P}_2|
results.quote: Proposition 1. IASM is in XP when parameterized by any of k or b or |\mathcal{P}_1\oplus\mathcal{P}_2|.
Proposition 2. IHR is solvable in \mathcal{O}(n^{2.5}\cdot m^{1.5}) time, where n is the number of residents and m is the number of hospitals.
Proposition 3. IHR-T is solvable in \mathcal{O}(n^{2n}\cdot nm) time.

results.bound: W[1]-hard when parameterized by m even if |\mathcal{P}_1\oplus\mathcal{P}_2|=1
results.quote: Theorem 3. Parameterized by the number m of hospitals, IHR-T is W[1]-hard even if |\mathcal{P}_1\oplus\mathcal{P}_2|=1.
Proposition 4. IHR-T is in XP when parameterized by the number m of hospitals.
Proposition 5. ISM-T is solvable in \mathcal{O}(2^{(t_U+1)\cdot(t_W+1)}\cdot n^{2.5}) time, where t_U respectively t_W is the number of agent types of men respectively women in P_2.
